extraction.summary: Atlas Retail Solutions runs a 310K-line hybrid ASP Classic/WebForms/MVC POS platform. Target is .NET 8 Blazor Server on Azure containers. October audit deadline drives urgency. Key risk: single developer holding stored procedure knowledge. Phased migration recommended starting with MVC-equivalent POS and inventory flows.

recommendedActions: Deliver Phase 1 SOW scoped to POS and inventory flows on .NET 8 Blazor within 3 months to meet October audit deadline
Schedule a knowledge-capture session with the senior stored procedure developer before any engagement starts to de-risk key-person dependency
Produce a written modernization roadmap document (3 phases) that Atlas can present to their enterprise customer auditors as a credible deliverable
Confirm Azure region preference and whether Atlas has existing Azure subscriptions or needs greenfield provisioning
Propose a discovery/architecture sprint (2 weeks) to validate the prototype Blazor Server + WASM island architecture before full Phase 1 commitment
discoveryQuestions: Which Azure region do your enterprise customers require for data residency or latency compliance?
What is the current user concurrency at peak — how many simultaneous sessions does the POS platform handle?
Is the database currently on-premises SQL Server, or already on Azure SQL or another managed service?
Has the senior stored procedure developer been formally interviewed or is departure still a risk — and has any documentation effort started?
What does 'credible demo' mean to the auditors — a live environment, a recorded walkthrough, or a written architecture attestation?
Are there any PCI-DSS, SOC 2, or other compliance frameworks driving the security audit beyond the enterprise customer requirement?
What is the approved budget range for Phase 1, and who holds budget authority — Patrick, a CFO, or a procurement committee?
objectionsToPreempt: Three months is too short for a real migration — address by scoping Phase 1 to only the POS and inventory flows (~30% of codebase) as a demonstrable pilot, not full migration
We already have an internal team — position GAP Velocity as augmentation and knowledge transfer, not replacement, especially for stored procedure archaeology
Cost is too high for a phased program — anchor ROI to the revenue at risk from losing the enterprise customer (70% revenue product) and the cost of continued technical debt
salesStrategy.roiNarrative: Atlas risks losing a major enterprise customer — and the 70% revenue product that depends on it — if they cannot demonstrate a modern, auditable architecture by October. GAP Velocity's phased modernization approach delivers a credible Phase 1 in time for the audit while protecting the team from key-person risk and positioning Atlas to hire modern .NET talent at scale.
salesStrategy.closePlan: Deliver Phase 1 SOW and 3-phase roadmap document by end of week. Schedule executive review with Patrick and Lisa to align on budget and sign-off path. Target SOW signature within 2 weeks to preserve October delivery window.
salesStrategy.strategySummary: This is a time-pressured rescue modernization with a hard October audit deadline and a single-developer key-person risk. Lead with a fixed-scope Phase 1 SOW covering POS and inventory flows to satisfy the auditor. Anchor the business case on protecting the 70% revenue product. Patrick (VP Eng) and Maria (Architect) are both engaged and technically aligned — move fast to SOW.
